proposal_title: Deletion of GenerationJob.track_mode from Canonical Domain Schema
domain_specific_rationale: From the Flow Browser Specialist (R06) perspective, removing track_mode from the canonical GenerationJob domain entity schema is entirely sound. Whether a generation task is executed via Track A (Playwright/Chrome MV3 worker) or Track B (FlowKit bridge) is strictly an operational routing and worker dispatch concern handled dynamically by R08 Google Flow Adapter and runtime dispatchers. Embedding track_mode into the canonical domain entity unnecessarily polluted core business entities with transient transport details and would have forced artificial database mutations whenever dynamic failover between Track A and Track B occurred. Deleting track_mode cleanses the domain model, maintains strict domain-infrastructure separation, and preserves complete freedom for browser worker pools to execute adaptive track switching behind the FlowExecutionPort interface.
capability_impact: Preserves CAP-01 (Canonical Core State Integrity) and CAP-18 (Track A / Track B Port Equivalence) by removing operational infrastructure coupling from canonical entity definitions while maintaining dynamic worker dispatch flexibility.
residual_risk: Downstream analytics queries monitoring Track A vs Track B performance distribution cannot rely on a static database column on GenerationJob. Mitigated by R14 OpenTelemetry tracing attributes (avf.worker.track) emitted during each FlowExecutionPort operation.
